data.long_meaning: Pradyotna means 'light' or 'lustre' in Hindu tradition. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Pradyotna', which refers to something that illuminates. The name Pradyotna carries the meaning “Light or Lustre” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pradyotna usually hope their child will grow to embody light or lustre and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Pradyotna was a legendary king mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata. He was the king of the Haihayas, a powerful dynasty in ancient India. Pradyotna is known for his great valor and justice, and he was a generous and noble ruler. He was a descendant of the lunar dynasty and ruled in the region of Mathura in present-day Uttar Pradesh, India.

Pradyotna was also a king in medieval Orissa, India, who ruled during the 13th century CE. He is known for his military prowess and his efforts to expand the territories of his kingdom. He is mentioned in various Orissan inscriptions and texts, including the Dhauli Inscription, which records his military victories.
